THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER

The petitioner-accused No.5 is before this Court seeking grant of bail under Section 439 of Cr.P.C.,
in Crime No. 101/2024 of Bengaluru CEN Crime Police Station, pending in on the file of the learned Chief Judicial Magistrate (CJM), Bengaluru Rural District, Bengaluru registered for the offences punishable under Sections 66 (C) and 66 (D) of Information Technology Act and Section 419, 420 of Indian Penal Code (for short 'IPC') on the basis of the first information lodged by the informant- Sri.Santhosh Kumar.
2. Heard Sri. Ram Singh K, learned counsel for the petitioner and Smt. K.P. Yashodha, learned HCGP for respondent -State.

sentences.text: Perused the materials on record.

3. In view of the rival contentions urged by the learned counsel for both the parties, the point that would arise for my consideration is:
"Whether the petitioner is entitled for grant of bail under Section 439 of Cr.P.C.?"
NC: 2024:KHC:21177

My answer to the above point is in 'Affirmative' for the following:
REASONS 4.
The petitioner - accused No.5 is seeking grant of bail.
He was apprehended on 04.04.2024, since then he is in judicial custody.
The complainant lodged the first information about cheating and criminal breach of trust.
Accused Nos.1 to 6 were apprehended.
It is stated that accused Nos. 1 and 4 were released on default bail.
Accused Nos.3 and 6 were granted bail.
5. It is the contention of learned counsel for the petitioner that the petitioner is also entitled for parity and to be released on bail.
However, it is the contention of learned High Court Government Pleader that the allegations made against the petitioner and the allegation made against accused Nos.3 and 6 are different.
Moreover, accused Nos.1 and 4 were released on default bail.

Therefore,
petitioner is not entitled for the benefit of parity.
The investigation is already completed and the charge sheet is filed.
It is stated that further investigation under Section 173(8) of Cr.P.C is undertaken and since it is a cyber crime some more details are required to be secured.
In the charge sheet serious allegations are made against the present petitioner stating that he collected the amount from various customers and an amount of Rs.3,51,245,078/- was received by him.

It is stated that the said amount was received in the account Shahnawaz vs State Of Karnataka By on 14 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/29608571/
2 of accused No.4.

sentences.text: It is the present petitioner through his mobile phone has transferred the amount to various other accounts and with the help of accused No.6 transferred the amount to the person in Malaysia.
The charge sheet further discloses that the Bank details transaction held by accused No.5 is yet to be collected.

However, the fact remains that accused Nos.1, 3, 4 and 6 are already enlarged on bail and even though accused Nos.1 and 4 were released on default bail, the prosecution has not sought for cancellation of bail after filing of the charge sheet.
The investigating officer will be at liberty to take the petitioner to custody with the permission NC: 2024:KHC:21177 of jurisdictional Magistrate.
Hence, I am of the opinion that at this stage the petitioner is entitled for grant of bail on parity 7.

In view of the above, I answer the above point in the affirmative and proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition is allowed.

The petitioner is ordered to be enlarged on bail in Crime No. 101/2024 of Bengaluru CEN Crime Police Station, on obtaining the bond in a sum of Rs.2,00,000/- (Rupees Two Lakhs only) with two sureties for the likesum to the satisfaction of the jurisdictional Court, subject to the following conditions:
a).
The petitioner shall not commit similar offences.
b). The petitioner shall not threaten or tamper with the prosecution witnesses.
c). The petitioner shall appear before the Court as and when required.

NC: 2024:KHC:21177 d) If in case, the investigating officer deems it necessary to subject the petitioner for custodial interrogation, he is at liberty to do so with prior permission from the jurisdictional Magistrate.
If in case, the petitioner violates any of the conditions as stated above, the prosecution will be at liberty to move the Trial Court seeking cancellation of bail.

On furnishing the sureties by the petitioner, the Trial Court is at liberty to direct the Investigating Officer to verify the correctness of the address and authenticity of the documents furnished by the petitioner and the sureties and a report may be called for in that regard, which is to be submitted by the Investigating Officer within 5 days.
The Trial Court on satisfaction, may proceed to accept the sureties for the purpose of releasing the petitioner on bail.
